correctness.rationale: The normalized right-half-plane Schwarz representation gives exactly M_α(ω), with |ω(z)|≤|z|. Exponential is injective on the closed unit disk, so the first boundary of exp(D) is mapped back by the Möbius inverse to the stated distance minimization. Its distance is less than one, already by testing w=−i for α≥0; hence a minimizing contact is attained in the parameter disk and a rotated Schwarz extremal realizes it. Inside exp(D) the inverse exponential agrees by normalization with the analytic logarithm. The squared distance is F_a(s), independent of the sign of Re w. Its derivative has the sign of Φ_a and the only possible endpoint denominator pole cannot minimize. Differentiating gives Φ'_a=(H''+H)cos(s+a), where H''+H=(v cosh v−sinh v)/v³ is positive with limit 1/3. On [−1,0] this gives strict increase, and the sign of Φ_a(−1) changes exactly once at the quoted angle. On [0,1] the derivative can switch only from positive to negative; the endpoint values rule out another minimum. These facts give exactly the two contacts below transition (including ±1 at zero angle), and one above and at it. Negative angles follow by conjugation. At transition the stationary branch reaches the endpoint transversely with F_ss>0 and F_as≠0. The optimized squared radius has matching first derivatives and positive second-derivative jump F_as²/F_ss, which transfers to the positive radius. For the small-angle law put N=cosh(1)−1, D=cosh(1)+1. Implicit differentiation gives s'(0)=−eN, and the minimized squared radius has quadratic coefficient N(2−eN)/D². Taking the square root gives the displayed coefficient; analyticity and reflection give the O(a⁴) remainder. Independent calculation reproduces the threshold and radii and confirms the coefficient; all continuum conclusions come from the signs and analytic derivatives, not from a grid.
residual_risks: At |α|=π/2 only the one-sided radius limit is claimed. Contacts are in logarithmic coordinates, and extremal equality is at |z|=R rather than inside it.

originality.rationale: A general first-boundary minimization theorem already yields the variational formula, and the same source or same target occurs separately in the closest publications. The distinct claim supported by the bounded comparison is the evaluation for this source–target pairing, with the exact angle threshold, equality-contact geometry, non-C² transition and expansion. No originality credit is assigned to the variational principle, the exponential target, or the single zero-angle value in isolation.
residual_risks: Comparison is not an exhaustive priority survey. Other worked examples of the boundary-minimum principle or equivalent rotated half-plane radius results may exist under different terminology.

value.rationale: The sharp universal radius for a standard spirallike class and a natural exponential starlikeness target is a motivated quantity. The exact global change from two extremal contacts to one, with its differentiability loss, distinguishes phenomena that a variational formula or a sufficient disk bound would not reveal. The result is useful at arbitrary permitted angles, not just at sampled values.
residual_risks: This is a result for one target; no transfer to other starlikeness regions is claimed.
